name: Heartwood Forest Community Orchard
description: A community orchard within Heartwood Forest, England's largest newly planted native woodland. Apple, pear and plum trees are open to the public for picking in season.

name: Birklands Meadow Community Orchard
description: An old meadow orchard rediscovered and restored by the Community Forest Association. Heritage apple and pear varieties, including local Hertfordshire selections, replanted in 1999.

name: Highfield Park Heritage Orchard
short_description: Spray-free heritage apple and pear orchard.
description: Two restored orchards managed without sprays by the Highfield Park Trust. Visitors are welcome to pick fruit in season, with an annual Apple Day event hosted each autumn.

name: Verulamium Park Wild Garlic
short_description: Spring garlic along the River Ver.
description: Carpets of wild garlic spread through the damp woodland edges of Verulamium Park each spring, particularly along the River Ver and around the ornamental lake margins.

name: Nomansland Common Blackberries
description: Nomansland Common's scrubby edges are rich with blackberry brambles, particularly around the Heartwood Forest boundary and the common's woodland fringe paths.

name: River Ver Watercress
description: The crystal-clear River Ver, a chalk stream, supports natural watercress beds along its course through St Albans. Pick small quantities from clear flowing water away from agricultural land.

name: Clarence Park Elder
description: Elder bushes thrive in the wilder borders of Clarence Park, offering fragrant flowers in early summer and dark berries in early autumn along the park perimeter paths.

name: Bernards Heath Hazelnuts
description: The hedgerows and scrubby woodland edges of Bernards Heath are dotted with hazel trees, offering good pickings of cobnuts and hazelnuts from late summer into autumn.

name: Sopwell Wild Plums & Damsons
short_description: Riverside wild plum and damson trees.
description: Scattered wild plum, damson and cherry trees grow along the old mill stream paths and hedgerows near Sopwell Nunnery ruins and the River Ver floodplain.

name: Incredible Edible St Albans - City Centre
description: Community-maintained planters in the city centre growing culinary herbs, salad leaves and seasonal vegetables, inspired by the Incredible Edible movement, free for all to harvest.

name: Batford Springs Wild Greens
description: The damp grassland and streamside margins of Batford Springs Local Nature Reserve support wild sorrel, watermint and ground elder, best gathered in late spring and early summer.

name: Sandridge Lane Rosehips & Haws
description: The old hedgerows flanking the lanes around Sandridge village are loaded with rosehips and hawthorn haws in early autumn — a classic Hertfordshire country lane picking spot.

name: Marshalswick Community Planters
description: Community edible planters near the local shops and green spaces of Marshalswick, growing herbs, kale and salad leaves for local residents to help themselves to freely.

name: London Colney Riverside Blackberries
description: Blackberry brambles grow thickly along the footpaths beside the River Colne at London Colney, with sloe-bearing blackthorn also present in the hedgerows further south.

name: Redbourn Common Sloes
description: Redbourn Common's ancient hedgerows are rich in blackthorn, making it one of the best sloe-picking spots in the district. Best harvested after the first frosts of autumn.

name: Highfield Park Community Orchard
description: Two large orchards (Hixberry and Cell Barnes) featuring hundreds of apple and pear trees open for community picking.

name: Incredible Edible St Albans - Civic Centre
short_description: Urban veg in the city heart.
description: Public planters outside the council offices and library featuring chard, kale, and aromatic herbs.

name: Heartwood Forest Hazelnuts
description: The newer plantings and existing ancient pockets contain a vast amount of hazel and dogwood.

name: Verulamium Park Wild Garlic
short_description: Spring ramsons by the River Ver.
description: The wooded banks of the River Ver, particularly near the Causeway, are thick with wild garlic in spring.

name: The Alban Way Blackberries
description: This disused railway path is a continuous corridor of blackberries and elder bushes from St Albans to Hatfield.

name: Bernards Heath Sweet Chestnuts
description: Mature sweet chestnut trees line the edges of the woods overlooking the historic heath.

name: Gorhambury Estate Sloes
description: The public footpaths through the estate are lined with blackthorn bushes (sloes) and hawthorn.

name: Batchwood Walnuts
description: Mature walnut trees can be found in the wooded borders of the golf course and public paths.

name: Clarence Park Rosehips
description: The perimeter shrubbery of the park contains many wild rose species for autumn hip gathering.

name: Sopwell Nunnery Wild Herbs
description: Feral herbs and wild mint often grow in the damp ground near the ruins and the river.

name: Sandridge Village Orchard
description: A small stand of mixed fruit trees planted by the local community for shared use.

name: Jersey Farm Woodland Elder
description: Abundant elder bushes for flowers and berries grow along the green lanes and woodland edges.

name: Ver Valley Meadow Sorrel
description: Find wild sorrel and watermint in the damp meadows heading south toward Park Street.

name: Fleetville Incredible Edible Planters
description: Planters featuring strawberries, chives, and mint near the community centre.

name: Redbourn Road Wild Plums
description: Several wild plum and bullace trees can be found on the wide verges of the old road toward Redbourn.
